stories.title: Desert Hawk Golf Course: what public records reveal about costs, debt and regional obligations
questions: What are Desert Hawk Golf Course's financial details?
Is Desert Hawk Golf Course profitable?
Can Desert Hawk funds pay for sheriff deputies?
stories.summary: County 2024 audited statements show $238,560 operating income but a $1,667,877 negative net position. Pueblo West’s 2025 audit lists $7,613,306 in long-term notes plus a $457,000 land option. Public records are spread across two institutions; no freely transferable balance is established. [S1,S2]

sources.title: Pueblo West 2025 ACFR — printed page 26 (PDF page 55)
Pueblo West May 2026 board summary — IGA and water explanation
County Desert Hawk board description and 2001 resolution
August 19, 2026 management board meeting — secondary summary, original minutes not verified
Pueblo West annual reports and budgets

chapters.heading: Public-source finding and scope
chapters.text: A supplied comment asks why Desert Hawk financial details have not been released. Annual financial details are available, although split across agencies. The county’s latest audited golf statements reviewed here are for 2024; Pueblo West’s 2025 audit supplies a newer creditor-side view. A missing 2025 county report does not erase the published records. [S1,S2,S8]

chapters.heading: Acquisition and purpose
chapters.text: The county acquired the course in 2000, citing recreation and preservation of area property values. Resolution 01-134, May 8, 2001, established a cooperative management board. The original 2005 acquisition-refinancing COPs were fully retired in 2024. Other obligations survive. [S1,S5]

chapters.heading: Management and responsibility
chapters.text: The official board registry lists seven seats, shared county/district appointments and the three county commissioners among members. A county enterprise fund reports the golf activity. Board membership is not evidence of personal wrongdoing. [S1,S5,S6]

chapters.heading: Operating results
chapters.text: 2024 customer/service revenue $1,531,007 less operating expenses $1,292,447 equals operating income $238,560 (15.58% margin). Income before transfers is $245,184; $45,322 transfers in raise net-position change to $290,506. Positive operating income does not establish financial independence or cash available to transfer. [S1 p25]

chapters.heading: Operating expense ledger
chapters.text: Contract fees $535,567; utilities and communications $323,820; supplies $193,504; depreciation $88,897; personnel $49,709; repairs/maintenance $42,995; insurance $30,038; professional services $27,522; equipment rent $395. These total $1,292,447; utilities includes more than water and contracts do not identify individual payees. [S1 p25]

chapters.heading: Assets, liabilities and net position
chapters.text: Assets $6,740,132 include cash $277,275, investments $898,089, net capital assets $5,076,762 and development land $457,000. Liabilities $8,396,323 plus deferred inflows $11,686 result in net position −$1,667,877; unrestricted net position −$6,699,928. Book values are not appraisals or sellable cash. [S1 p24]

chapters.heading: Cash flow and retired financing
chapters.text: Operating cash flow $340,307; transfer receipts $45,322; capital/financing cash outflow $730,750 (including $580,000 COP principal); investing net outflow $94,890. The net decline is $440,011, from $717,286 to $277,275 cash. The county narrative says General Fund transfers were not needed for COP repayment in 2024, yet the enterprise statements show a transfer in; origin and purpose require reconciliation, not an assumption of operating subsidy. [S1 pp9,26]

chapters.heading: County obligation breakdown
chapters.text: At end 2024 county reports $6,334,553 non-interest-bearing loan, $1,279,813 water advance, $457,000 purchase option; total $8,071,366. Other current obligations include $212,715 due to other funds; do not add a second copy of the district receivable to regional debt. [S1 pp24,66]

chapters.heading: Newer district-side evidence
chapters.text: 2025 Pueblo West audit lists $6,078,478 historical operating/debt-service note, $255,000 acquisition/other note and $1,279,828 water note; total notes $7,613,306, plus $457,000 land option = $8,070,306. It reports notes not scheduled to be collected the subsequent year. County 2024 versus district 2025 totals differ by $1,060; dates and classifications differ, and no repayment can be inferred solely from that difference. [S2 p26]

chapters.heading: Water cost and counterevidence
chapters.text: The IGA treats water not covered by annual revenue before 2011 as noninterest-bearing loans and provides untreated water at no more than actual district cost. District’s May 2026 statement says the golf course has paid under agreement terms since 2011. Hence $8.07M is not an ordinary overdue water bill. Current consumption, rate, metering and repair costs require independent comparison. [S1,S2,S3]

chapters.heading: Repayment and event horizon
chapters.text: Repayments are limited to excess revenues over cash disbursements and $500,000 per year for all applicable loans. For the 2025 district notes alone (excluding land option), illustrative constant annual payments $100k, $250k, $500k imply 77, 31, 16 payment years, assuming no further advances or changes and all payment directed to those notes. These are bounds/scenarios, not an enforceable amortization schedule. [S1,S2]

chapters.heading: 2027 budget and decision
chapters.text: County slides project 2026 ending budgetary balance $1.29M, 2027 revenue $1.82M, expense $1.55M and ending $1.56M, all millions. The 2026 inputs are unaudited. An August 19 secondary meeting summary reports equipment reductions and fee decisions; verify original minutes before relying on contract/fee changes. [S4,S7]

chapters.heading: Water infrastructure and asset choices
chapters.text: Investigate irrigation replacement, lifecycle cost, measured losses and water affordability. Secondary meeting summary reports infrastructure discussion, but no leak estimates or funding claims are treated as verified. Compare retain/reinvest, competitively contract, restructure IGA, lease, sell or change use only after appraisals, legal review, access and debt/land-option protections. [S7]

chapters.heading: Public safety crossover
chapters.text: Do not count the $1.56M projected golf budgetary balance, the $7.61M notes or the sale book value as freely available sheriff funds. Assess legal authority, obligations, deferred maintenance, debt repayment priorities, revenue loss and recurring net effect separately. Compare golf recreation and affordability, water affordability, emergency resources and child/family effects without assuming service tradeoffs are zero.

chapters.heading: Q processing, LL, EE and T2Y
chapters.text: Retain fiscal date, entity, fund, accounting basis, item, counterparty, value and source page; match district assets to county liabilities only at common dates. Record public statements as attributed, do not replicate commentary identities. Reuse audited rows across budget, water, debt, regional twin and public asset packets; review contradictions rather than overwriting them.

chapters.heading: RX, implementation and future
chapters.text: Build an asset/IGA packet with ownership, financing, repayment, transfers, water volumes and lifecycle maintenance; publish costed alternatives and annual totals. Trigger review at 2027 budget adoption, next County ACFR and any IGA amendment, then year 3 and 5 repayment/capital comparisons. Human decision authority remains with participating governments. No automated financial action.

unknowns: County 2025/2026 audited enterprise results, transfer counterparties and final 2027 appropriation not verified.
Current IGA amendments, repayment schedule, actual water usage, deferred maintenance, appraisals and contractor payments not reconciled.
Pueblo West 2025 audit text retrieved; page screenshot failed. County key pages and budget slide were visually verified.
No finding of illegal subsidy or legally transferable funds.

stories.title: Pueblo County’s budget realities: reconstructing the commissioners’ public explanation
questions: What is the commissioners' explanation for the Pueblo County budget crisis?
Do Pueblo County's 2027 budget graphics reconcile?
How much did county detention expenses increase?
stories.summary: Commissioner-shared graphics describe capital commitments, declining marijuana revenue and rising service costs. Recalculation shows $19.068M lower proposed revenue/sources versus the 2026 budget, with lower grants and zero proposed financing accounting for $17.928M of that net change. A proposed $1.265M surplus is a narrow margin, not a final result.

sources.title: County official budget portal — preliminary book and presentations
County October 2026 proposed budget presentation, slide 9 and other slides
County 2024 ACFR — governmental fund and debt statements
County November 2026 progress and policy report
Pueblo Ledger November 14 — secondary description of preliminary budget

chapters.heading: Evidence intake
chapters.text: Nine supplied screenshots include a resident question and overlapping captures of a post attributed to Commissioner Paula McPheeters crediting CAO Robert Choi’s 2027 preliminary budget. Deduplicate repeated graphics; do not add overlapping engagement numbers. The post showed 16 reactions, 4 comments and 15 shares in one capture, not a representative survey. The original post and full preliminary PDF could not be independently retrieved. Figures attributed to screenshots are labeled separately from audited or verified documents.

chapters.heading: Administration's explanation
chapters.text: The post argues the county faces structural problems: historical capital projects, debt service, sustained marijuana receipts decline and higher recurring costs. These can all be real pressures; historical authorization and current budget management are different responsibilities. The original jail refinancing claim concerns initial financing, not every later amendment or payment. [S1–S5 and supplied graphics]

chapters.heading: Capital and debt
chapters.text: Supplied capital graphic: governmental capital outlays were $10.9M in 2021, $21.2M in 2022, $36.8M in 2023, $118.85M in 2024; debt payments in 2024 $19.83M. 2024 capital outlays are about 10.9 times 2021. Capital spending, financing principal and current operating expense are distinct. The graphic identifies jail/roadway, Workday and Beulah water as commitments; project-specific award, funding source, contract changes and actuals are not established by totals alone.

chapters.heading: Marijuana revenue
chapters.text: Supplied graph: 2019 $6.0M, 2020 $13.7M, 2021 $14.3M, 2022 $9.3M, 2023 $7.9M, 2024 $6.6M, 2025 $5.39M (rounded graph $5.4M). It reports a 62.3% peak-to-2025 fall, $8.90M lower revenue and rate change from 3.5% to 6% in 2020. Four consecutive lower receipts following 2021 are a planning warning; no conclusion about individual knowledge or intent follows. These are combined tax streams, not all unrestricted General Fund revenue.

chapters.heading: Revenue reconciliation
chapters.text: Displayed totals $116,960,406 / $141,734,585 / $122,666,601. Row sum for 2025 is $116,960,405, a $1 difference; 2026 and 2027 reconcile exactly. 2027 is $19,067,984 below 2026 budget; grant decrease $12,427,888 plus financing decrease $5,500,000 = $17,927,888 (94.02% of net decrease). Property decreases $1,896,852; sales rises $18,000. These are proposal-versus-budget changes not actual losses or proof grant funds could pay for eligible personnel.

chapters.heading: Recurring revenue nuance
chapters.text: 2025 recorded total includes $3.686M financing, whereas 2027 proposal has zero financing. Proposed total is $5,706,195 greater than the displayed 2025 recorded total; excluding financing, difference $9,392,195. Grants/transfers may still be temporary or restricted, so these comparisons do not establish a structural operating surplus. Do not compare preliminary 2025 recorded numbers as audited actuals.

chapters.heading: Six cost drivers
chapters.text: Supplied graphic, 2023 actual / 2025 recorded: property/liability insurance $967,345 / $1,658,262; detention medical $4,656,465 / $5,894,700; health claims/admin $13,404,845 / $15,879,224; utilities $2,410,939 / $2,674,738; repairs/maintenance contracts $395,586 / $1,017,949; detention overtime $1,779,099 / $2,445,239. Total $23,614,279 to $29,570,112 = $5,955,833 increase (25.22%).

chapters.heading: Detention crossover
chapters.text: Medical increase $1,238,235 (26.59%) plus overtime increase $666,140 (37.44%) = $1,904,375, or about 32% of the selected cost rise. These are gross cost areas, not the whole sheriff budget or verified causal effects of the new jail. Health claims/admin is shown before reimbursements. Connect staffing, custody demand, city–county agreements, contracts and health coverage; do not count these increases twice.

chapters.heading: Budget exact arithmetic
chapters.text: Supplied graphic lists revenue/sources $122,666,601; base expenditures $131,213,309; reported base shortfall $8,546,709; reductions $9,811,472; proposed expenditures $121,401,837; reported surplus $1,264,763. Recalculation gives shortfall $8,546,708, expenses $121,401,837, surplus $1,264,764. Two one-dollar differences likely underlying precision/rounding; not evidence of lost money. Reported surplus is 1.031% of proposed revenue.

chapters.heading: Margin stress test
chapters.text: Holding other items constant, 1% revenue loss $1,226,666 leaves about $38,097 of reported surplus. 90% attainment of the $9,811,472 reduction gives $283,616. Budget-balance headroom is not evidence that reserve targets or services are adequately funded. Do not combine annual shock with the separately projected opening balance.

chapters.heading: Opening balance and fiscal policy
chapters.text: October slide 9 expressly says the opening balance incorporates $7M anticipated asset sale and $15M anticipated COP. No financing in the 2027 annual revenue table does not contradict possible 2026 financing. Separate years and verify transactions. County progress report says policy sets 10% minimum and 16.67% target; subsequent schedule and exact eligible reserve measure need confirmation. [S2,S4]

chapters.heading: Inherited versus current governance
chapters.text: Assign each project original authorization, later amendments, new financing, approved budget, expenditure, forecast and operating handoff to independently dated resolutions. The 2024 audit documents lease obligations but alone does not establish a complete responsibility matrix. Do not accuse a named official or exonerate all current decisions solely from the graphic. [S3]

chapters.heading: Options and child impact
chapters.text: Compare recurring-cost controls, contract renewal, job vacancy treatment, debt and capital plans, restricted grant continuity and public safety service assessment. Evaluate prevention, detention healthcare, staffing, child reporting/education services and families receiving grants. No confirmed equivalent savings or causal harms claimed.

chapters.heading: Q processing, LL, EE, T2Y and shadow
chapters.text: Record screenshot-derived rows as source observations, not final audit figures; retain original display totals and recalculated sums. Version the November communications, match the original budget and audit when available, never overwrite historical figures silently. Reuse data across pension, public safety, jail, Desert Hawk and regional packets; separate staff time saved from cash savings.

chapters.heading: RX, procurement and leap
chapters.text: Require project authorization packets with 10–30 year debt, operations, staffing, maintenance, revenue sensitivities, contract commitments and exit plan; review Workday interoperability before new technology spending. A full-cost capital plan and monthly exception dashboard can help prevent reconstruction. Test read-only on historical figures; human authorization required.

chapters.heading: Event horizons
chapters.text: Before final 2027 budget adoption, update figures and alternatives; publish actual-vs-budget plus debt and grant reconciliation monthly in 2027. Compare reserve progress, recurring income and service outcomes through 2029 and 2031. No claim these practices are fully implemented. [S4]

unknowns: Original post and complete preliminary budget book inaccessible; screenshot figures are attributed, not independently audited.
2025 audited actuals, 2026 actual results, project-by-project costs and grant-specific restrictions not reconciled.
Actual service reductions, final budget and financing transactions unverified.
